newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude prices ease in thin local talk.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude prices ease in thin local talk.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices fell in quiet Thursday trade, softened by lower crude prices in other regions and minimal local interest, traders said.
Most West Coast refiners had finished buying July barrels earlier this week, with discounts at $2.16 under July West Texas Intermediate.
Higher volumes of imports, weak refinery margins out West, and excess sellers have weakend prices.
With discounts unchanged, the regional benchmark, Alaska North Slope (ANS), fell in sympathy with lower crude prices in other regions.
The grade's main seller, BP, offered cargoes at $1.85 under July deliveries of WTI, the U.S basis for cash and futures oil markets.
Outright prices for ANS were $16.49/16.69 a barrel, down 15 cents in line with WTI cash markets.
One small refiner in the U.S Northwest still needed to buy oil but considered cutting runs instead of taking ANS barrels.
Heavier California grades fell Thursday after major oil companies lowered postings.
